description: Add OpenAI-Compatible custom endpoint support - allows users to configure any OpenAI-compatible server (Ollama, LM Studio, OpenRouter, etc.) with a custom base URL, API key, and model name.
steps: Step 1 - Backend: Add CUSTOM_OPENAI to EngineId enum in backend/app/schemas/common.py.
Step 2 - Backend config: Add custom_openai_api_key, custom_openai_base_url, and custom_openai_model fields to Settings in backend/app/config.py (all default to empty string).

Step 3 - Backend deps: Add custom_openai field to Byok dataclass in backend/app/deps.py. Add x_byok_custom header param to get_byok(). Add for_custom_openai() method to KeyResolver. Update ENGINE_TO_BYOK.

Step 4 - Backend provider: Create backend/app/providers/custom_openai.py - a lightweight wrapper around the OpenAI chat completions pattern. It accepts base_url, api_key, and model as parameters (passed at call time, not hardcoded). Implement translate_bubbles() only (no vision/OCR since we cannot guarantee the user's model supports it). The implementation should be nearly identical to openai.py's translate_bubbles() but with configurable _API_URL.

Step 5 - Backend pipeline: Update backend/app/services/pipeline.py to handle CUSTOM_OPENAI as a translation-only engine (like DEEPSEEK). The custom base URL and model should be read from request headers or config. Add X-Custom-Base-Url and X-Custom-Model headers to pass these values from the frontend.
Step 6 - Backend deps update: Add custom_base_url and custom_model fields to Byok dataclass, extracted from X-Custom-Base-Url and X-Custom-Model headers.
Step 7 - Backend translate router: Add CUSTOM_OPENAI case to backend/app/routers/translate.py.
Step 8 - Frontend types: Add 'CUSTOM_OPENAI' to the EngineId union in types.ts.
Step 9 - Frontend auth store: Add customOpenaiApiKey, customOpenaiBaseUrl, and customOpenaiModel fields with setters to useAuthStore.ts. Persist all three.
Step 10 - Frontend API client: Add custom field to ByokKeys. Add X-Byok-Custom, X-Custom-Base-Url, X-Custom-Model to byokHeaders() (only when custom values are present).

Step 11 - Frontend settings modal: Create features/settings/CustomOpenAISettingsModal.tsx with fields for: Base URL (text input, placeholder 'http://localhost:11434/v1'), API Key (password input, optional), Model Name (text input, placeholder 'llama3'). Use a teal/cyan color theme.

Step 12 - Frontend pipeline integration: Update useTranslatePipeline.ts to read customOpenaiApiKey/customOpenaiBaseUrl/customOpenaiModel from store, include in buildByok(), and add credential check (require at least baseUrl and model).
Step 13 - Frontend cost estimation: Add CUSTOM_OPENAI with { input: 0, output: 0 } pricing (user's own infra).
Step 14 - Frontend App.tsx: Import CustomOpenAISettingsModal, add state/modal, add CUSTOM_OPENAI to translator <select>, add settings button, render modal. Add 'custom' case to onAuthError.
Step 15 - Update planPipeline.ts to handle CUSTOM_OPENAI as translate-only (not OCR-capable).
acceptance_criteria: CustomOpenAISettingsModal.tsx exists with Base URL, API Key, Model Name fields
X-Byok-Custom, X-Custom-Base-Url, X-Custom-Model headers are sent when configured
findings: All 15 steps implemented successfully. 28 tests pass. TypeScript compiles cleanly. Production build succeeds. CUSTOM_OPENAI added as translation-only engine (not in OCR dropdown). Custom endpoint requires base URL and model name; API key is optional for local servers like Ollama. Settings button added to sidebar grid with teal color theme.
